title: Effectivity and simultaneous descent of quotient realization models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L\subset M$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure, allowing equality, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_F$, uniformizers $\varpi_F$, and $A_{F,n}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes considered have $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On fixed small skeletons of their pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], put $R_{F,W}=\lim_n(A_{F,n})_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use ordinary unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathscr S_F(W)$ for strict quotient-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, $\mathcal R_{F,W}$ for derived reduction, and $\mathcal L_{F,W}=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for realization, with their specified whole-system adjunction $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$ and actual unit $u$ and counit $e$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

Use $U_{f,F},S_{L/E,W},\widehat U_{f,F},\widehat S_{L/E,W}$ as defined in [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems, def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. A derived quotient system is normalized if $C_m\otimes^L_{A_{F,m}}A_{F,n}\to C_n$ is invertible for all $m\ge n$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Put $\mathcal C_F(W)=D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_F)$, with the derived completeness, bounded constructible reductions and single uniform cohomological interval of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Fix the normalized Roos, unit and counit constructions of [lem-trf-roos-adjunction-quotient-normalization] and the primitive quotient-complex comparisons $\alpha,\beta$ of [lem-trf-primitive-quotient-realization-comparisons].

For any scheme map $f:X\to Y$ and ambient $K\in D(R_{E,Y})$, the reduction system $\mathcal R_EK$ is normalized. Exact whole-system inverse image preserves its transition-adjoint isomorphisms, using the canonical identification $f^{-1}(A_{E,n})_Y\cong(A_{E,n})_X$; hence $U_{f,E}\mathcal R_EK$ is normalized. The scalar system $S_{L/E,Y}\mathcal R_EK$ is normalized as well, including ramified extensions. Their realizations are derived complete, and their actual counits $e$ are isomorphisms in the derived category of the entire strict quotient diagram. If $K$ is derived complete, its actual completion unit $u_K$ is invertible. These assertions concern the fixed maps computed by the K-injective projections and zero-shifted quotient augmentation, not merely the existence of levelwise isomorphisms.

If moreover $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$, the completed pullback $\widehat U_{f,E}K$ lies in $\mathcal C_E(X)$ and the completed scalar extension $\widehat S_{L/E,Y}K$ lies in $\mathcal C_L(Y)$. Transport along the primitive comparisons $\alpha,\beta$ puts the two system realizations in those same categories, with bounded constructible reductions in one interval independent of $n$.

The primitive comparisons descend naturally to derived functors simultaneously for every scheme, map and coefficient inclusion, with all quotient transitions retained. Concretely, a quasi-isomorphism between flat-term K-flat representatives induces quasi-isomorphisms on both pullback and scalar Roos complexes; their canonical descended-functor comparisons agree on common refinements. The scalar association is independent of the representative as a coherent system comparison. The comparison $\rho$ is natural on the derived category of whole towers and independent of K-injective resolutions. Consequently the primitive comparisons, which are composites of these comparisons, commute with every representative change and common refinement. The counit is the natural transformation of the specified whole-system adjunction, so computing it with another K-injective tower resolution gives the same morphism. These comparisons arise from strict quotient maps or whole-diagram functors before taking the limit. The transition and tensor-generator identities for $E\subset L\subset M$ therefore survive localization, and one gets simultaneous descended models with exactly the normalization in [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. No flatness or finite Tor bound on $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,n}$ is used.

proof.text: The well-definedness theorems give quasi-isomorphism invariance and their chosen normalized functors give the unique comparison-preserving descended functor isomorphisms. Naturality of alpha, beta and the actual counit gives the three displayed squares. primitiveQuotientRealizations_unique gives uniqueness of the two primitive realizations. For Roos comparisons, every tower complex has a K-injective replacement. Their computes fields agree on that replacement, and naturality and cancellation along the localized replacement identify their inverse comparisons on every complex. For the final normalized Roos descent choose H to be coefficientConstantTowerLimit itself, kappa the inverse fixed comparison and rho the identity. The required formula is the identity law; cancel kappa and use faithfulness of precomposition with the localization Q to prove comparison-preserving uniqueness.

retained_arguments.text: The reduction system $\mathcal R_EK$ is normalized by [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps]. Its whole-system inverse image is normalized by the inverse-image clause of [lem-pur-system-normalized-tensor-closure], applied to the pro-etale inverse-image morphism and the constant quotient coefficient sheaves. Their identification with the target constant sheaves is part of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. The scalar system $S_{L/E,Y}\mathcal R_EK$ is normalized by [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model], which applies to arbitrary ambient $K$ and explicitly permits ramification. Apply [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps] separately over $E$ on $X$ and over $L$ on $Y$: both realizations are derived complete and their actual counits $e$ are isomorphisms in the derived categories of whole strict systems. When $K$ is derived complete the same node makes its actual unit $u_K$ invertible. Thus effectivity concerns the actual maps fixed in Steps 2 and 5; it is not inferred merely from the existence of some levelwise isomorphisms.

retained_arguments.text: Now let $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] the completed pullback $\widehat U_{f,E}K$ belongs to $\mathcal C_E(X)$. By [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] the completed scalar extension $\widehat S_{L/E,Y}K$ belongs to $\mathcal C_L(Y)$. The primitive isomorphisms constructed in Steps 3 and 4 identify these with the two realizations in the statement. Hence those realizations have the required bounded constructible reductions and the single uniform cohomological interval of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. These two preservation statements have precisely the arbitrary scheme-map and finite coefficient-extension hypotheses in force here. No separate flatness or finite Tor-amplitude assumption on the finite quotient coefficient map is inserted.

source.place: Final sentence, integral comparison underlying common finite coefficient stages; constructibility is supplied by the cited preservation theorems

retained_arguments.text: Finally descend the construction simultaneously. A comparison between flat-term K-flat representatives is sent to a quasi-isomorphism of pullback Roos complexes by [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], and to one of scalar Roos complexes by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. Both nodes give descended functors and canonical comparison isomorphisms compatible with every K-flat representative. Scalar association is independent of the representative as a coherent system comparison by [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model]. The comparison $\rho$ is natural on the derived category of whole towers and independent of K-injective resolutions by [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. Thus the primitive maps are composites of these natural comparisons, so commute with every change of representative and with a common refinement. The counit is already a natural transformation of whole-system derived functors, by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; its representative formula in Step 2 computes that fixed transformation on any resolution. Consequently changing a tower resolution also leaves it unchanged. All these comparisons are formed before the limit from strict quotient maps or from functors of the whole diagram. They retain every quotient transition. Use this single Roos functor, this fixed adjunction, and these comparisons for each field and scheme; the generator identities in Step 4 hold on any simultaneous representative and survive localization. They therefore give the simultaneous models of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models], with the asserted natural descent.

lean.statement: theorem effectiveQuotientModelDescent {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (_hlX : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (l : X.residueField x)) (_hlY : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (l : Y.residueField y)) (SY : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E Y) (SX : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X) (SL : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l L Y) (ρX : IntegralComparisonRoosModel l E X) (ρL : IntegralComparisonRoosModel l L Y) : (∀ K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E Y), IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence l E Y (SY.reduction.obj K) ∧ IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence l E X ((integralComparisonDerivedSequencePullback l E f).obj (SY.reduction.obj K)) ∧ IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence l L Y ((integralComparisonDerivedSequenceScalar l E L ι Y).obj (SY.reduction.obj K)) ∧ IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E X none ((coefficientSequenceLimit l E X).obj ((integralComparisonDerivedSequencePullback l E f).obj (SY.reduction.obj K))) ∧ IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l L Y none ((coefficientSequenceLimit l L Y).obj ((integralComparisonDerivedSequenceScalar l E L ι Y).obj (SY.reduction.obj K))) ∧ IsIso (SX.adjunction.counit.app ((integralComparisonDerivedSequencePullback l E f).obj (SY.reduction.obj K))) ∧ IsIso (SL.adjunction.counit.app ((integralComparisonDerivedSequenceScalar l E L ι Y).obj (SY.reduction.obj K))) ∧ (IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E Y none K → IsIso (SY.adjunction.unit.app K))) ∧ Nonempty (IntegralComparisonPullbackModel l E f SY ρX) ∧ Nonempty (IntegralComparisonScalarModel l E L ι Y SY ρL)
